NAME(S):  


# Fitch-Margoliash Exercise

Consider four gene sequences, (A, C, D, E), having the following distance matrix:


\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25}
\begin{table}[H]
\begin{tabular}{|p{1cm}|p{1cm}|p{1cm}|p{1cm}|p{1cm}|}
\hline
  & A  &  C  & D & E \\ \hline
A & -  &  -  & - & - \\ \hline
C &  39  &  -  & - & - \\ \hline
D &   39 & 18    & - & - \\ \hline
E & 41 &  20 & 10 & - \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
\end{table}


1.	Use UPGMA to determine kinship between the four sequences.  What can you use as an outgroup?

\vspace{8em}


\vspace{2em}



2.	Using the three most related sequences, figure out appropriate branch lengths using the Fitch-Margoliash algorithm and draw the resulting *unrooted* scaled tree.

\vspace{8em}


\vspace{2em}


3.	Use the outgroup along with the Fitch-Margoliash algorithm to create a phylogram: a *rooted* scaled tree with appropriate branch lengths for the three most related sequences.
